# Veqtor MCP

> Veqtor is a local, open-source MCP server that gives compatible AI clients defined tools for working with tracked changes in Microsoft Word documents.

Public v0.5.0 technical Alpha: fourteen tools under veqtor.mcp.v0.5.0; macOS and Linux; Python 3.12-3.14; Claude Code on macOS/Linux; Claude Desktop on macOS.

What Veqtor can do:
- find Word negotiation drafts in deterministic filename order;
- read supported tracked text changes;
- inspect accepted/current main-body text with exact paragraph references;
- map exact paragraph evidence and recorded document-byte derivations;
- trace one paragraph backward across a complete declared file order using exact matches;
- check wording against a specific tracked change or paragraph, with current or explicitly selected rejected-pending paragraph text;
- test a complete proposed edit batch before writing;
- create a separate Word document with supported tracked changes;
- make exact text edits in supported clean paragraphs and table cells;
- save and restore negotiation positions, conditional fallbacks and open business questions for a later round;
- export a compact local activity record for the legacy document workflow;
- edit supported text under a configured author and re-edit that author’s own pending insertions;
- read ordinary comments, add anchored comments, and update or delete the configured author’s own comments;
- save author-drafting edits to the working path with an exact backup, or create a new copy.

Important boundaries:
- Claude supplies reasoning and drafting; Veqtor supplies document facts and defined writes.
- Veqtor does not provide legal advice.
- Legacy counterproposal tools create a separate output and never overwrite the source or an existing destination. Author drafting can save to the same path with a required exact backup; another existing destination is never overwritten. Close Word before saving, reopen afterwards and refresh references. Word and sync software do not share Veqtor’s lock.
- It is not a generic Word editor or a tamper-evident audit system.
- Headers, footers, footnotes, accept/reject, Windows and hosted MCP are outside v0.5.0. Comment replies and resolve/reopen are not provided; complex, threaded or rich comment mutations may be refused. Saving requires a supported local filesystem.
- The three author-drafting tools return record_status=disabled and do not append the legacy activity journal. Backups and individual results support recovery, not a complete negotiation history.
- Saved positions are confidential local data, separate from the activity journal. Confirmation is specific to a displayed version and does not authorize later edits or settle business decisions. Copies do not synchronize automatically.
- Paragraph history is not semantic lineage or verified chronology. Ambiguous or unresolved steps stop backward propagation.
- Rejected-pending wording is a mechanical reading, not a recovered original or a proven prior round. Literal author and date metadata remain unverified.
- Text returned to the AI client may be processed by the user's model provider under that provider's terms.
